title: El-Sayed Disinvites Former Primary Opponent Haley Stevens from Detroit Event as Rift Deepens
snippet: With just days left before Election Day, Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has disinvited former primary rival Rep. Haley Stevens from a joint campaign appearance in Detroit amid escalating public clashes over Israel.
content:
In a clear sign that primary tensions have failed to cool, Democratic Senate candidate Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has pulled the plug on a planned unity appearance with his former rival, Rep. Haley Stevens, just days before Michigan voters head to the polls.

El-Sayed disinvited Stevens from a scheduled Sunday event at a Detroit church, where the two were set to share the stage alongside veteran South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn. According to a source familiar with the decision, El-Sayed’s team wanted to prevent ongoing bickering with Stevens from overshadowing his platform during the critical final stretch of his high-stakes Senate campaign against Republican nominee Mike Rogers.

A Fractured Show of Unity

The Detroit appearance was intended to showcase party solidarity following a contentious August primary, which El-Sayed won by a narrow margin. However, the fragile truce dissolved after Stevens publicly criticized an ad run by an independent progressive group that blamed Israeli aid for rising domestic costs, including grocery and healthcare prices. Stevens demanded El-Sayed condemn the ad and apologize for similar rhetoric he has used on the campaign trail.

El-Sayed quickly fired back, accusing Stevens of clinging to a primary battle that concluded months ago. He urged Michigan Democrats to stay laser-focused on defeating Rogers, holding Donald Trump accountable, and reforming campaign finance rather than rehashing old rivalries.

High Stakes for the Home Stretch

Foreign policy, particularly support for Israel, served as a major flashpoint during the Democratic primary and continues to reverberate into the general election. Stevens received millions in financial support from pro-Israel political action committees during her primary run, while El-Sayed—a prominent progressive critic of Israeli military policy—has consistently advocated for a halt to U.S. foreign aid to the nation.

The persistent intra-party tension comes as Republicans look to seize on Democratic divisions. Rogers has actively courted disaffected Democratic voters, particularly within Michigan's Jewish community. Illustrating the dynamic, while Stevens maintains that she still plans to cast her ballot for El-Sayed, her fiancé, who is Jewish, recently announced he will be voting for Rogers.
